title: How Long Does Therapy Take to Work?
description: Realistic timelines for therapy results. When to expect improvement, how many sessions you'll need, and how to know if it's working.

content.text: You've started therapy. Now you're wondering: how long until I feel better? Here's what research and clinical experience tell us.
Research shows 50% of patients improve significantly within 15-20 sessions. By session 26, that rises to 75%.
content.citation: Hansen et al., Clinical Psychology Review, 2002

content.text: For most people with depression or anxiety, meaningful improvement happens within 3-6 months of weekly therapy.

items: 8-16 sessions of CBT typically
Improvement often noticeable by session 4-6
Maintenance or booster sessions may follow
8-12 sessions of trauma-focused therapy (PE, CPT, EMDR)
May feel worse before better (processing trauma)
Improvement usually evident by session 6-8
12-20 sessions of ERP (Exposure and Response Prevention)
Intensive formats available (daily sessions)
Significant reduction in symptoms is realistic
Often 1-2+ years
Progress may be gradual
Focus on long-term change, not symptom relief
You're thinking about your problems differently
You're doing things you'd been avoiding
Your worst days aren't as bad
You're using techniques outside sessions
You feel understood by your therapist

content.text: Feeling temporarily worse (especially early on) doesn't mean therapy isn't working. Processing difficult emotions is part of the work.
If after 6-8 sessions you see no improvement at all:

items: Discuss this openly with your therapist
Consider whether the approach is right for your issue
Evaluate the therapeutic relationship
Ask about adjusting the treatment plan
Consider a different therapist or modality
Severity and complexity of issues
How long you've had the problem
Trauma history
Support system outside therapy
Consistency of attendance
Homework completion (for CBT)
Quality of therapeutic relationship

content.text: Most people feel meaningfully better within 3-6 months of weekly therapy. Give it at least 8-12 sessions before deciding it's not working. Therapy is an investment—but for many people, it's the most important investment they'll ever make.
